rounds.text: Yogi Ltd is demonstrating explosive top and bottom-line acceleration, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 296% and a staggering profit growth of 1342% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This fundamental strength is translating into superior profitability, with filed statements showing a robust ROE of 16.7% and ROCE of 12.8% [E13, E12], significantly outperforming sector medians like an ROCE of 6.1% [E52]. Insiders and management are putting their money where their mouth is, as promoter holdings have increased by 13.02 percentage points from 49.66% in September 2023 to 62.68% in June 2026, alongside an additional 1.59% increase over the last quarter [E29, E37]. Furthermore, the business is becoming significantly more efficient, successfully cutting its working capital requirements from 241 days down to 114 days [E38]. The balance sheet remains a pillar of strength with a conservatively financed debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.13x [E26], positioning the company well ahead of its distressed sector benchmark which sports an ROA of -105.06% [E8]. Conceded: [E22, E23, E24].

Yogi Ltd trades at an extreme valuation premium that is entirely disconnected from its fundamental reality, evidenced by a lofty P/E of 57.9x against a sector benchmark of 24.42x and a P/B of 5.22x [E1, E6, E7]. This rich pricing leaves no margin of safety, as a discounted cash flow analysis places intrinsic value at Rs 66 per share compared to a market price of Rs 168, generating a negative margin of safety of -155.4% [E31, E32]. Compounding these valuation concerns, the business suffers from severe operational cash flow destruction, bleeding Rs -192 Cr in free and operating cash flow for March 2026, which translates to an alarming cash conversion rate of -9.14x relative to reported profit [E22, E24]. Underlying quality is further undermined by high debtors stretching to 282 days and a weak median ROE of 8% over a three-year period [E20, E42]. The rules-based screen reflects these fundamental disconnects by scoring the stock a 42 out of 100 with a sell recommendation at medium confidence [E43]. conceded: [E14]

While the bear flags an elevated P/E of 57.9x and a DCF value of Rs 66 [E1, E31], this static valuation misses explosive top and bottom-line momentum where compounded sales growth reached 296% and profit growth hit 1342% [E14, E15]. Profit growth is radically outperforming 1-year price growth by 1346%, signaling that the market is only just beginning to appreciate accelerating fundamentals [E35]. Although operating cash flow dipped to negative Rs 192 Cr [E23], the company aggressively slashed its working capital requirements from 241 days down to 114 days, demonstrating active operational turnaround [E38]. The long-term return profile is robust with an ROE of 16.7% and a recent median ROE peaking at 17%, substantially outperforming historical three-year medians and crushing sector benchmarks [E9, E13, E21]. Furthermore, insiders are heavily backing this growth trajectory as promoter holding increased significantly by 13.02 percentage points overall and another 1.59% over the last quarter to reach 62.68% [E29, E37]. conceded: [E22]

The bull points to explosive top and bottom-line momentum with compounded sales growth at 296% and profit growth at 1342% [E14, E15], but this is severely undermined by a net profit decline of 126% YoY and decelerating earnings growth [E45, E46]. While the bull highlights working capital improvements down to 114 days [E38], it glosses over persistently alarming operational metrics, specifically high debtors stretching to 282 days and a dangerous risk that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E41, E42]. The assertion that market price lags behind fundamentals is contradicted by a steep P/E of 57.9x and a P/B of 5.22x that heavily outprice sector benchmarks, alongside a negative DCF margin of safety at -155.4% [E1, E2, E6, E7, E32]. Conceded: [E29]. Although the bull emphasizes a 16.7% ROE [E13], the rules-based screen scores the company a mediocre 42 out of 100 with a medium-confidence sell signal due to a low historical 3-year median ROE of 8.33% and extreme cash burn [E23, E40, E43].
